summary: Bridget Allchin was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Cape Town (~1946–1950). She founded the European Association of South Asian Archaeology and Art in 1970 and held a post at Wolfson College (~1977–2017).
Brigitte Marschall studied at the University of Vienna (~1976–1983). She later served as Professorin at the University of Vienna (~2000–2022).

Bronislaw Malinowski studied at the Jagiellonian University, Leipzig University, and the London School of Economics under Charles Gabriel Seligman. He held academic posts at the LSE (~1913–1938), Cornell University (~1933), and Yale University (~1939–1942).

Bronwyn Finnigan, a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies, studied at Auckland, Sydney, and Melbourne. She held posts at Auckland (~2008–2013), Marquette (2012–2014), and the Australian National University (2014) as continuing lecturer and deputy head of philosophy.

Brook Ziporyn, a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD at Michigan under Donald J. Munro and studied at Chicago. He held posts at Northwestern (~2003–2013), National University of Singapore (~2012–2013), and Chicago (~2013).
Brooke Schedneck is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Arizona State University under the supervision of Juliane Schober.

Bruce Charles Williams is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He was taught by Edward H. Schafer, Michael Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, Akira Fujieda, and Noritoshi Aramaki.

Bruce John Stewart specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Sakya College in 1978 and earned his PhD at Columbia University, where he was supervised by Alex Wayman and taught by Joel Peter Brereton and Christopher S. George.

Bruce Lincoln, specializing in religious studies, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studied at Haverford and Chicago under Mircea Eliade (~1970–1976). He held posts at the University of Minnesota (~1976–1992) and the University of Chicago (~1992).

Bruce Matthews, a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, pursued graduate studies at McMaster University (~1971–1974). He held posts at the University of Ceylon and Acadia University (~1976–2006), where he was C. B. Lumsden Professor of Comparative Religion.
Bruce McCoy Owens works in religious studies and Indology. He held posts at Columbia University (attested 1988) and at Wheaton College as associate professor of anthropology (attested 2019).
Bruno Dagens was an Indology and archaeology scholar who studied under Colette Caillat. He served as a professor at KU Leuven (~1977–1986).
Bruno Galasek is a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

Bruno Liebich was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Kielhorn (~1883–1886). He served as Professor Ordinarius at the University of Breslau (~1891–1921) and held a post at Heidelberg University (~1921–1928).
Bruno Lindner was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Rudolf von Roth (~1874–1878). He held a post at Leipzig University from ~1879 to 1925.

Bryan D. Lowe is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at Otani University and with Jacqueline I. Stone. He held a post at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017).

Bryan J. Cuevas, a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, earned his PhD at Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. He held a fellowship at Princeton and a professorship at Florida State University (attested 2008–2021).
Bryce Ryan held academic posts at Cornell University and the University of Ceylon.

Bulcsu Siklós, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, completed a PhD at the University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski and Charles R. Bawden. He held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 1996).
Bunkyo Aoki, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, was a disciple of Kozui Otani (~1910–1916). He held a post at the University of Tokyo (~1942–1946).
